name: Phosphene Variations (The Uncut Feed)
description: An experimental neural-feed film by artist-director Ossian Ferreira-Mbeki in which the viewer has no protagonist body — they exist as diffuse sensory data flowing through the BCI infrastructure of a single city block over 72 hours of compressed time. The experience induces genuine synesthesia, involuntary emotional states, and a documented phenomenon called 'mesh grief' — mourning for strangers whose data you briefly inhabited. Licensed in limited quantities due to mental health flagging by corporate wellness boards.
cultural_impact: Redefined what neural-feed cinema could do with perspective and permanently influenced a generation of experimental filmmakers who began calling themselves the Diffuse School.
story_hooks: A viewer of the film believes they experienced a genuine crime being committed during the 72-hour timeline — a memory too specific and detailed to be fictional
Ossian Ferreira-Mbeki has been approached by a corponation offering unlimited funding for a sequel — the terms of the contract are deeply strange
The 'uncut feed' version circulating underground is 40 minutes longer than the licensed cut and contains a segment that licensed viewers have no access to
